spans.quotation: We considered the Announced Pledges Scenario (APS) from the International Energy Agency's (IEA's) World Energy Outlook (WEO) 2024 in conducting our analysis. The WEO uses a model to estimate the future supply, demand, and prices for oil and natural gas under various hypothetical scenarios. The APS is based on the assumption that all of the climate commitments made by countries, industries, and companies around the world, including Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) and net zero targets, will be achieved in full and on time and illustrates how far current pledges will go in helping to reach the Paris Agreement's goal of limiting global average temperature increases to well below 2°C.

Our analysis used a reference case model for our companywide operations running through 2040. To be conservative, we did not assume that successful exploration will add to our current inventory. Other assumptions used to develop our reference case model included the following:
• A commodity price outlook for our U.S. inventory determined by the APS pricing assumptions beginning in 2030 and based on strip pricing in earlier years, which averaged $68.10 Brent per barrel of oil ($64.00 West Texas Intermediate equivalent per barrel of oil) and $3.29 per million Btu of natural gas over the life of the scenario.
• Carbon dioxide (CO2) taxes in advanced economies of $135 per metric ton beginning in 2030 and growing to $175 per metric ton by 2040, as forecasted by the APS. The reference case model used projections for our U.S. Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG emissions. These assumptions resulted in additional costs that grow to approximately $3.30 per Boe by 2040.

We further stress-tested our reference case model using a flat commodity price of $50 per barrel of oil and $2 per thousand cubic feet of natural gas in place of APS pricing assumptions. Using the same CO2 tax and dividend growth assumptions, and modified production growth assumptions, the more conservative commodity price scenario still yielded significant profitability and free cash flow. We believe the results of the analysis confirm the resiliency of EOG's portfolio against climate-related risks to long-term commodity pricing and demand.

note: criteria 1, 3, 4 — 3 of 5. Criterion 1 (quantitative grounding) satisfied: carbon tax assumption of $135/metric ton CO2 in 2030 growing to $175/metric ton by 2040 stated explicitly; commodity price assumptions of $68.10 Brent/bbl and $3.29/MMBtu natural gas over the scenario life named; resulting additional cost impact of approximately $3.30/Boe by 2040 disclosed; stress-test prices of $50/bbl and $2/Mcf stated — all constitute specific quantitative assumptions and outputs. Criterion 2 (target-bound) not satisfied: no named resilience target with baseline and target year is stated; the analysis confirms portfolio resilience but does not commit to a named quantitative resilience metric with a baseline. Criterion 3 (methodology disclosed) satisfied: named scenario (IEA WEO 2024 APS) with explicit description of its assumptions; reference case model covering companywide operations through 2040; conservative no-exploration-upside assumption stated; strip pricing methodology for pre-2030 period named; APS pricing methodology for post-2030 period named; free cash flow requirement used as the resilience test; stress-test overlay with alternative commodity prices described — together these constitute a stated scenario methodology with named inputs, structure, and output metric. Criterion 4 (time horizon) satisfied: 2040 analysis horizon explicit; 2030 policy implementation start date named; 2024 reference base confirmed. Criterion 5 (progress tracking) not satisfied: per handbook explicit pitfall, trend_disclosed is never true for S3; scenario projections are not historical multi-year performance metrics; no multi-year comparison of scenario outputs across reporting years is disclosed. scenario_linked = true: IEA WEO 2024 Announced Pledges Scenario (APS) is explicitly named — this is on the handbook allowed list ('APS (Announced Pledges), WEO scenarios with explicit name'). trend_disclosed = false: confirmed per handbook pitfall. uncertainty_discussed = true: p.18 acknowledges uncertainty in timing and scale of climate-related efforts; p.20 states 'The scenarios we evaluated are not predictions of the future' and describes the conservative no-upside assumption as a methodological acknowledgment of uncertainty. Boundary calls: (a) the quantitative outputs ($3.30/Boe cost, resilience conclusion) also inform S1 risk magnitudes — cross-concept noted; (b) response measures referenced in the scenario context (net zero ambition, emissions targets) belong to S4 and M5 respectively. Additional disclosure on p.84 confirms three IEA WEO 2024 scenarios are referenced (APS, Stated Policies, NZE by 2050) though only APS is used in the primary analysis.
